findings.description: This creates a persistent IAM user access key rather than using federated, temporary credentials. Long-lived keys are susceptible to theft and remain usable until manually disabled or rotated.

The policy grants full EC2, S3, Lambda, and CloudWatch permissions against every resource. These broad service-wide permissions violate least privilege and can enable data access, infrastructure modification, and privilege escalation depending on resources in the account.

The IAM access-key secret is emitted as a Terraform output without `sensitive = true`. It can therefore be displayed in CLI output and exposed to users or systems able to read Terraform outputs/state.
